search_angle: metrology + sensor ontology + inverse-problem identifiability + open-source uncertainty software

projections.projection: metrological traceability is a property of a measurement result connected to a reference through a documented calibration chain, with calibration uncertainty contributing along the chain
the measurand is inferred through a measurement model from input quantities rather than being identical to an instrument indication
instrument calibration alone is insufficient to establish traceability of a measurement result; traceability also does not imply fitness for a particular use

projections.source: W3C Semantic Sensor Network Ontology — 2023 Edition
projections.projection: observation, observable property, feature of interest, sensor/system, procedure and result are distinct semantic roles
sensor layout and experiment design bound identifiability and uncertainty in an inverse problem, so observational informativeness is observation-design dependent

projections.source: PTB measurement uncertainty software / PyDynamic / GUM2DFT
projections.projection: open-source metrology software explicitly propagates uncertainty through dynamic transforms instead of treating transformations as uncertainty-free

deduplicated_retained_objects: measurement-aware similarity certificate distinct from generic structural witness
observation equivalence indexed by probe family, tolerance, operator/model, uncertainty, resolution and regime
same observable explicitly non-authoritative for mechanism/generator/target truth
